image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) resting on a bed of green moss and dark soil near a rock. The salamander has a glossy black body with distinct, irregular bright yellow patches and spots. Its skin appears wet and textured. The head is visible with small eyes, and the limbs are tucked against the body. The tail extends towards the right side of the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with the species, appearing broad. While the specific glandular texture is hard to resolve at this resolution, the general morphology and swelling behind the eye area match the description of parotoid glands.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are visible but appear as flat, dark beads without discernible depth or the characteristic gold-flecked iris detail. They lack the 'protruding' quality described in the taxonomy, looking more like painted dots than biological structures.
